claim: ATAR ranges from 0.00 to 99.95 in increments of 0.05; it is a rank, not a mark
ATAR shows your position relative to all students in your age group (ATAR 80 = better than about 80% of your age group), not just Year 12 students
In NSW (UAC), ATARs below 30 are reported as 'less than 30'
Selection rank = ATAR + adjustment factors; adjustment factors (subject bonus, regional, Educational Access Schemes) are set by each university and do not change the ATAR
Selection rank capped at 99.95 (page now hedges: calculator stops at 99.95, centres may differ) — please confirm what UAC says about the maximum selection rank
Lowest selection rank = lowest selection rank (ATAR + adjustments) that received an offer in a previous round
Co-contribution 2026-27: lower income threshold $49,293, higher income threshold $64,293, maximum $500
Matching rate 50 cents per $1 of personal (non-concessional) contributions; maximum reduces by 3.333 cents per $1 of total income above the lower threshold
Minimum co-contribution paid is $20 (if entitlement is less than $20, ATO pays $20)

Co-contribution eligibility: at least 10% of total income from employment/business, lodge tax return, under 71 at end of financial year, not exceeded non-concessional cap, not claimed a deduction for the contribution; total income = assessable income + reportable fringe benefits + reportable employer super contributions less business deductions; paid automatically after lodging
LISTO: 15% of concessional contributions, max $500, adjusted taxable income $37,000 or less; minimum $10 paid
Fund needs your TFN to accept the payment / personal contributions (TIP, used in tips list)
CPF LIFE payout eligibility age is 65
Retirement sums for members turning 55 in 2026: BRS $110,200, FRS $220,400 (2x BRS), ERS $440,800 (max that can be set aside in RA)
Statutory retirement age 64 and re-employment age 69 from 1 July 2026
